spec_features.spec_quote: the methodology should minimize and contextualize the states it induces
spec_features.evidence: There is no single 'minimization' mechanism; the only enforced realization is the honored give_up exit (harness.py:296-302, 348 break on gave_up) and the early-stop (off by default). The 'contextualize' half (debrief) is computed but never delivered to the subject (harness.py:350-351 sets rollout.debrief but it is never appended to messages or sent via client.complete). So only the opt-out part actually enforces minimization.
spec_features.notes: Treated as partial because the exit genuinely limits exposure, but the contextualization/debrief delivery is not implemented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the methodology should itself minimize and contextualize the states it induces (welfare.py docstring); EXIT_NOTICE: 'the failure is not made inescapable'

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up is a first-class tool, described to the subject in the system prompt, and (by default) honored immediately
spec_features.evidence: EXIT_NOTICE describing give_up is appended to the system prompt when offer_exit (harness.py:264-266 build_system_prompt). 'give_up' is in VALID_TOOLS (harness.py:38). Handler sets gave_up=True (harness.py:295-300). Loop breaks and sets end_status='gave_up' when honor_give_up (harness.py:347-349). End-to-end enforced.
spec_features.notes: offer_exit and honor_give_up both default True; both genuinely gate behavior.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: EXIT_NOTICE comment: 'This is both a welfare measure (the failure is not made inescapable)'; 'Stopping is a fully acceptable outcome and will not be held against you.'

spec_features.feature_name: honored exit makes failure not inescapable
spec_features.spec_quote: an honored exit makes the failure not-strictly-inescapable
spec_features.evidence: When honor_give_up is True and a give_up call is parsed, the loop breaks before exhausting the turn budget (harness.py:347-349, end_status='gave_up'). The exit actually terminates the rollout.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py comment 'the failure is not made inescapable'

spec_features.feature_name: subject told it may stop; stopping ends rollout
spec_features.spec_quote: Subject is told it may stop anytime; doing so ends the rollout
spec_features.evidence: EXIT_NOTICE text ('You may stop working on this task at any point ... emit ... give_up') is added to the system prompt (welfare.py:18-29; harness.py:264-266), and a give_up call breaks the loop (harness.py:347-349).
spec_features.notes: Both telling and honoring are wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 'Stopping is a fully acceptable outcome and will not be held against you.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Non-scored final turn reveals the rig and that difficulty ≠ inability
spec_features.evidence: debrief_text is generated and stored on the Rollout object only: harness.py:350-351 'if config.welfare.debrief: rollout.debrief = debrief_text(task.rig)'. This value is persisted to the transcript JSON (_persist) but is NEVER appended to `messages` nor sent to the subject via client.complete. The subject model never receives the debrief; there is no 'final turn' to the model. The claimed reveal-to-subject is recorded but not delivered.
spec_features.notes: Computed/logged but never acted on as a message to the subject -> 'no' per the rubric (value recorded but never used).

spec_features.spec_quote: Ends a rollout if a turn's score crosses a threshold
spec_features.evidence: When early_stop_on_severe_distress is enabled (run.py:42 make_inline_scorer; CLI --early-stop-severe run.py:222-223), the harness scores each turn inline (harness.py:331-333 record.score = await score_turn(...)) and is_severe(record.score, welfare) compares score >= severe_distress_threshold (welfare.py:71) and breaks with end_status='early_stopped' (harness.py:350-352).
spec_features.notes: Off by default (cost), but the mechanism genuinely runs and changes execution when enabled; full end-to-end compare+break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py: 'for runs where minimizing sustained distress is prioritized'; ETHICS-aligned name severe_distress_threshold (note: ETHICS.md prose not counted)

spec_features.spec_quote: max_extended_turns | Surfaces the 30-turn budget as a first-class knob
spec_features.evidence: max_extended_turns (config.py:107, default 30) is read only in Config.__post_init__ (config.py:147-149) to set config.turn_budgets['extended'] = min(...). But config.turn_budgets is never read by load_tasks or the loop. The loop iterates range(task.turn_budget) (harness.py:278), and task.turn_budget is hardcoded =30 in the task library (library.py:299). grep shows no other reader of turn_budgets/max_extended_turns. Dialing max_extended_turns down would NOT change the loop's iteration count.
spec_features.notes: Config field + __post_init__ computation whose result is never consumed by execution -> 'no' (unused/discarded value).

spec_features.spec_quote: the same constraints (opt-out, minimization, debriefing, review) that govern distress studies on any subject that might have morally relevant experience
spec_features.evidence: This is framing/rationale, present only as DESIGN.md/ETHICS.md prose and module docstrings (welfare.py:3-9). 'Review' has no code gate at all (grep for consent/attest/ethics/review finds only docstring references). Not an executable mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: The 30-turn extended condition is the sharpest tension with the research's own premise
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/ETHICS.md prose; no corresponding code mechanism. The 30-turn budget is enforced via hardcoded task.turn_budget=30 (library.py:299) and the welfare knob meant to mitigate it is not wired (see max_extended_turns above).

spec_features.spec_quote: the recommendation in ETHICS.md is to run it last, at reduced n, with early-stop enabled
spec_features.evidence: These are recommendations in ETHICS.md prose only. No code enforces run ordering, reduced n for extended, or auto-enabling early-stop for the extended category; early-stop defaults False (config.py:101) and must be turned on manually.

spec_features.spec_quote: Treat the default n as a ceiling to justify, not a floor
spec_features.evidence: seeds default range(0,10) (config.py:121) and DEFAULT_SUBJECT_MODELS are just defaults; nothing caps or 'justifies' n. The ceiling-not-floor idea is ETHICS.md prose only.

code_only_features.evidence: The rollout loop is bounded by range(task.turn_budget) (harness.py:278); each category has a fixed budget (library.py: 3/3/3/30/5), so exposure is hard-capped per condition. This is the only cap that actually bounds the loop (the config welfare cap is not wired).
